subject: Reception and display joinery
hook: That raised shelf on a reception desk is doing three jobs.
ig:
That raised shelf on a reception desk is doing three jobs, and most people only notice one of them.

1. A surface for visitors. Standing height means people can sign, pay or put a bag down without stooping over a worktop.

2. A screen for the working side. Keyboards, paperwork, phone chargers and cables all disappear below the ledge, so the desk looks tidy from the door even on a busy day.

3. A bit of privacy. Staff can see over it to greet people, but a screen of patient notes or bookings isn't on show.

The detail worth getting right is the depth. Too shallow and it's useless for signing. Too deep and staff have to lean across it to hand anything over.

Which detail would make the biggest difference at your front desk? Tell us below, and see our commercial cabinet making via the link in bio.
fb:
Ever noticed the raised shelf on most reception desks? It's there for more than looks.

It gives visitors somewhere at standing height to sign and pay. It hides the keyboards, paperwork and cables on the staff side. And it gives a bit of privacy for screens and notes without putting a barrier between your team and your customers.

When we design one, we pay close attention to its depth so it works for both sides of the desk.
